Beginner's Guide Newly diagnosed
with a vascular anomaly?

Vascular tumors and malformations include many different diseases. Even under the same name, the course and treatment differ from patient to patient, so it can be hard to find the information you need.
Here, for patients and healthcare professionals alike, we explain diseases and treatments with the latest information, as clearly as we can.
Learn more

Understandthe disease

About vascular tumors & malformations

How do the diseases differ? Why are there so many names? What are the keys to telling them apart? And more.
We introduce the basics of vascular tumors and malformations.

Learn more

Types of vascular tumors & malformations

Vascular tumors and malformations come in several types;
here we explain them in seven categories.

Disease 01

Infantile Hemangioma
(strawberry hemangioma)

The most common vascular tumor in infancy, with a strawberry-like appearance.

Learn more
Disease 02

Vascular Tumors Other
Than Infantile Hemangioma

Rare vascular tumors that must be distinguished from infantile hemangioma.

Learn more
Disease 03

Capillary Malformation
(port-wine stain)

A flat red birthmark present from birth.

Learn more
Disease 04

Lymphatic Malformation
(lymphangioma)

Sacs of lymphatic vessels present from birth, often on the face or neck.

Learn more

Each disease has different
features and treatments.
Identifying which disease applies
is an important first step.

Department of Pediatrics, Gifu University Hospital
Michio Ozeki

Disease 05

Venous Malformation
(cavernous hemangioma)

A mass-like collection of blood vessels present from birth, often in the skin.

Learn more
Disease 06

Arteriovenous Malformation

A malformation in which arteries and veins are abnormally connected.

Learn more
Disease 07

Combined Vascular Malformations
(e.g. Klippel–Trenaunay syndrome)

Complex malformations combining veins and lymphatic vessels.

Learn more

Treatmentthe disease

Treating vascular tumors & malformations

Treatment options include surgery, laser therapy, endovascular treatment, conservative care, and more.
Here we focus on drug therapy, our research group's area of expertise.

Drug therapy

Resection surgery
(surgery)

Sclerotherapy

Laser therapy

Endovascular treatment
(embolization / sclerotherapy)

Conservative treatment
(compression therapy)

About SirolimusAbout sirolimus

Sirolimus is a new “molecular targeted” medicine that suppresses the cell signaling pathway underlying these diseases. Start here to learn what kind of medicine it is.

Learn more

About other candidatesMedicines other than sirolimus

Besides sirolimus, other medicines are also expected to be effective for vascular tumors and malformations.
